To: Executive Leadership and Regional Operations
From: Supply Chain Director
Date: [Insert Date]
Subject: Establishing a cost-effective shipping plan across our source and destination network

Situation
Our distribution network spans multiple warehouses, factories, and regional centers supplying a broad set of stores and customers. Transportation rates vary by lane, and origin capacities differ by location. To protect margins and maintain on-time service, we need a clear plan that aligns available inventory with destination needs while avoiding unnecessary freight spend.

Problem
We need a shipping plan that assigns volumes from each source to each destination so that:
- No origin ships more than its available inventory or processing capacity.
- Every destination receives its required quantity within the planning window.
- Total transportation spend is kept as low as possible given route-by-route costs.

Shipments must be in whole unit quantities; partial loads are not permitted. This adds complexity where exact matches are difficult, and may require careful allocation to avoid overages while fully covering demand. Costs differ by route, so we must leverage proximity and lower-cost lanes where feasible without compromising coverage or service.

Approach and Deliverables
- Use the supply, demand, and lane cost inputs in the Annex to evaluate feasible allocations across all origin–destination pairs.
- Produce a practical, lane-by-lane shipping schedule in whole units, indicating recommended volumes from each source to each destination.
- Report total expected freight spend and highlight any unused capacity or unmet demand (if any) for resolution.
- Flag high-cost lanes and potential consolidation or carrier procurement opportunities for further action.
- Coordinate with Operations and Procurement to validate service commitments, carrier availability, pickup/delivery windows, and any lane restrictions before execution.

Why this matters
- Cost savings: Directing flow to cost-effective lanes reduces total freight spend without adding complexity to operations.
- Service reliability: Ensuring each destination’s requirements are met sustains fill rates, on-time performance, and customer satisfaction.
- Transparency: A clear plan provides visibility to trade-offs and supports data-driven decisions on sourcing, carrier selection, and regional balancing.

Action requested
- Please review and confirm the accuracy of the data in the Annex and advise of any operational constraints (e.g., lane caps, mode restrictions, or lead-time requirements). Upon confirmation, we will finalize the shipping plan and circulate an execution-ready schedule.
